name: abiogenesis

phase_0.boundary_condition: The lipid vesicle membrane of the protocell establishing inside-outside asymmetry and concentrating polymers against diffusive entropy

VINIT.chosen_element: Prebiotic inorganic precursors (H₂O, NH₃, CH₄, H₂, CO₂, dissolved metal ions)
VINIT.justification: The undifferentiated chemical state before any organic complexity exists — Earth's primordial atmosphere and ocean prior to monomer synthesis

TANCH.chosen_element: Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA) with coupled genotype-phenotype and membrane-bounded metabolism
TANCH.justification: The terminal closure of abiogenesis — the first entity satisfying all criteria of life: self-replication, compartmentalization, and Darwinian evolution

AFWD.chosen_element: Energy-driven monomer synthesis via atmospheric discharge and UV photolysis forming amino acids and nucleobases
AFWD.justification: The upward-directed morphism from simple inorganics to complex organics driven by external energy input (lightning, solar UV)

AREV.chosen_element: Hydrothermal vent geochemistry with mineral surface catalysis and thermal gradient-driven condensation
AREV.justification: The descending morphism — alkaline vents provide geochemically reduced conditions and mineral templates (iron-sulfur clusters) that catalyze organic assembly without UV, representing an alternative descent pathway

CLINK.chosen_element: Peptide bond and phosphodiester bond formation linking monomers into heteropolymer chains
CLINK.justification: Sequential composition of monomers into polymers — each bond formation depends on the prior activated intermediate, creating an irreversible chain of growing molecular complexity

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-complementary RNA hairpin acting as both template and ribozyme catalyst
IMSCRIB.justification: The molecule that recognizes its own sequence — the RNA strand whose folded structure catalyzes templated ligation of matching oligomers, achieving molecular self-reference

FSPLIT.chosen_element: Template-directed replication separating one RNA strand into two complementary daughter strands
FSPLIT.justification: The co-multiplication operation δ — a single self-replicating RNA molecule produces two complementary single strands, each inheriting half the information of the original

FFUSE.chosen_element: Complementary strand re-annealing and ligation restoring the double-stranded replicating population
FFUSE.justification: The multiplication operation μ — the two complementary strands rejoin by Watson-Crick base pairing and phosphodiester ligation, recovering the original replicating RNA molecule with sequence information preserved (FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x)

EVALT.chosen_element: Functional ribozyme achieving catalytic turnover and template-directed ligation of cognate oligomers
EVALT.justification: The affirmative evaluation — a self-replicating RNA molecule successfully catalyzes its own replication, achieving positive feedback and information amplification

EVALF.chosen_element: Hydrolytic degradation and non-enzymatic thermal decay of RNA polymers
EVALF.justification: The negative evaluation — polymer chains break apart faster than they elongate, the error catastrophe threshold is exceeded, and replicating information is lost to entropic dissolution

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Protocell exhibiting both chemical self-organization and incipient Darwinian selection simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: The paradice — at the protocell stage, the system is simultaneously a thermodynamic dissipative structure (non-living physics) and a replicating population subject to selection (living biology), held in unresolved tension at the origin threshold

IFIX.chosen_element: Closure of the genetic code with universal codon assignments and coupled DNA-RNA-protein translation
IFIX.justification: The irreversible fixation — once the triplet code and the ribosome co-evolve, the genotype-phenotype mapping becomes locked and unbreakable, committing all descendant life to the same genetic language

phase_2.split_element: Template-directed RNA strand separation into complementary daughters
phase_2.split_input: One self-replicating RNA molecule carrying sequence S
phase_2.fuse_element: Watson-Crick re-annealing with ribozyme-catalyzed phosphodiester ligation
phase_2.fuse_result: Restored self-replicating RNA molecule carrying sequence S — information content preserved exactly (FFUSE(FSPLIT(S)) = S)

phase_3.void_description: Dissolved inorganic molecules in equilibrium with ambient conditions — no chemical gradients, no organic complexity, no informational states
phase_3.true_description: Self-replicating protocell population with ribozyme-catalyzed template-directed replication, net positive growth rate, and selectable phenotypic variation
phase_3.false_description: Hydrolyzed monomer soup below the threshold for sustained polymerization — molecules degrade faster than they assemble, no replicating information persists
phase_3.both_description: Protocell at the lifedeath boundary — simultaneously a self-maintaining dissipative structure and a replicating population, satisfying criteria of both prebiotic chemistry and biology before either framework can exclusively claim it

steps.domain_action: Prebiotic inorganic precursors fill the primordial ocean and atmosphere — no organic molecules, no gradients, no information
Lightning discharges and solar UV radiation drive Strecker synthesis and HCN oligomerization forming amino acids and nucleobases
Alkaline hydrothermal vent effluent provides H₂, HS⁻, and dissolved Fe/Ni sulfide minerals creating steep pH and redox gradients
Amino acids undergo condensation on mineral surfaces forming short peptide chains; nucleotides undergo template-directed ligation
An RNA hairpin folds into a pseudoknot structure that base-pairs with complementary oligomers — the first self-referencing molecule
The self-complementary RNA strand undergoes strand separation driven by thermal fluctuation, producing sense and antisense templates
Ribozyme catalytic pocket achieves 3′-5′ phosphodiester bond formation on cognate template, yielding a full-length complementary copy
Competing hydrolysis at elevated temperature cleaves phosphodiester bonds faster than ligation can repair — net information loss
Complementary strands re-anneal via Watson-Crick pairing and ligase ribozyme seals nicks — the original replicating RNA is recovered exactly
Thermochemical synthesis at hydrothermal vents produces fatty acids and isoprenoid alcohols as amphiphilic precursors
Amphiphilic molecules self-assemble into bilayer vesicles at the ocean-sediment interface driven by hydrophobic effect
RNA polymers become encapsulated within lipid vesicles — covalent polymer chains compose with non-covalent membrane assembly
The protocell is simultaneously a thermodynamic self-organization (non-living) and a replicating lineage (living) — both states held without resolution at the origin threshold
Encapsulated ribozyme replicates the genome inside the protocell, generating two copies of the informational RNA
Replication rate exceeds vesicle division rate — the protocell lineage achieves net positive information propagation
Vesicle osmotic lysis or membrane destabilization releases contents — the protocell population collapses
Daughter vesicles inherit both membrane lipids and replicated RNA from the parent protocell — the lineage continues intact
A ribozyme evolves that catalyzes peptide bond formation on an RNA template — the genetic code begins to self-reference its own translation products
Peptide polymers fold into stable tertiary structures and provide catalytic function that supplements ribozyme activity
LUCA emerges with a complete coupled system: lipid membrane, RNA genome, ribozyme-derived ribosome, primitive genetic code, and membrane-bound energy conservation via chemiosmotic proton gradients
The universal genetic code becomes frozen — all viable descendants inherit the same triplet codon assignments, making the code an append-only irreversible record of the origin event

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Thermodynamic disequilibrium at hydrothermal vents translates geochemical energy gradients into organosynthesis and polymerization operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Non-covalent base pairing, hydrophobic lipid self-assembly, and proton gradient chemiosmosis coordinate information flow between genome, replicase, and membrane
phase_5.memory_mechanism: RNA sequence information stored as 3′-5′ phosphodiester oligomer chains; lipid composition stored in the self-assembling bilayer; proton gradients stored as transient electrochemical potential
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Temperature-dependent reaction kinetics and vesicle growth-division cycles determine the temporal ordering of synthesis, replication, and compartmentalization operations
phase_5.alfs_store: The universal genetic code and the LUCA genome reconstruction — the canonical reference from which all extant life traces its informational descent

phase_6.cycle_cost: Geochemical free energy consumed per replication cycle: H₂, HS⁻, and dissolved inorganic carbon drawn from hydrothermal effluent
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Primordial inorganic soup with dissolved gases and mineral surfaces — equilibrium-bound, no organic complexity, zero biological information
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Self-replicating protocell population with encapsulated RNA genomes, peptide catalysts, and lipid membranes — far from equilibrium, sustaining continuous information propagation against diffusive and hydrolytic decay
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS > 0 globally but ΔS ≈ 0 locally within the protocell — the vesicle maintains its internal low-entropy state by continuously dissipating geochemical free energy from the hydrothermal gradient, exactly offsetting the hydrolytic and diffusive entropy production
